correctness.rationale: The simplex Gram matrix has off-diagonal -1/d and eigenvalue n/d on its d-dimensional row space; every size-k sub-Gram matrix is positive definite. Its ones-eigenvalue (d-k+1)/d gives z_S and norm squared delta^2*k*d/(d-k+1). Permutation symmetry and trace give E[P_S]=k/d I, E[z_S]=0 and E[z_S z_S^T]=delta^2*k/(d-k+1) I. Since Q_S z_S=0, the conditional squared-error recurrence is exact, hence its solved transient and stationary formulas hold for every d,k,t. Isotropy of the covariance at an LS initialization follows by induction. The included exact rational script checked all subsets for d=2..7 and every k; these finite checks are not substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: The established noisy sketch-and-project inequality gives a convergence neighborhood, whereas the present result gives equality at every finite iteration and the full covariance for every uniformly sampled subset size in a minimal-redundancy tight frame. The exact strict block-size reversal, including a dimension-factor gap and covariance isotropy, was not located in inspected relevant full-text sections or indexed mathematical claims. Priority remains qualified by the possibility of an older unindexed equality-case computation.
residual_risks: The newest general sketch-and-project proof is close to the present conditional second-moment equality; an unindexed explicit regular-simplex equality case may be prior.
Older block iterative-projection literature not exhausted, and some related sources were compared via accessible summaries rather than full text.
Finite exact tests diagnose arithmetic but do not establish novelty or mathematical proof for all dimensions.

value.rationale: The regular simplex is the natural minimally redundant unit tight frame: its entire observation inconsistency is the common-mode residual, so the calculation classifies all noisy response vectors in that family. It shows an exact, strictly monotone and dimension-unbounded tradeoff between noiseless contraction and actual least-squares error floor, and also yields the entire finite-time covariance. This is useful for testing block-size heuristics in noisy projection solvers without confusing bias in the least-squares target with iteration noise. It makes no claim about general frames or computational cost.
